judged_text: updateEvent's fallback branch compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, the previous code fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId; now every Google event update on such a booking sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API and fails, breaking reschedule/location-edit of pre-refactor bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback branch), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so it will not match a real calendar externalId and returns `undefined`. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now an array), so this change can cause updates to lose the intended calendar selection for bookings without `externalCalendarId` references (pre-refactor), likely leading to updating the wrong calendar (e.g., defaulting elsewhere) or failing with 404.
